title: Corner: Scripted Demo Environment Spec
summary: Full spec for a self-running scripted demo at aheadofmarket.com/demo. Pre-recorded story, no backend needed, any prospect can run it anytime. Removes the bottleneck of Patrik needing to be on every call.
content:
Corner: Scripted Demo Environment Spec

Author: Steve (Sales Director) Date: 2026-03-22 For: Bobby (builder), Steffen (visual direction) Priority: P1 -- ships after S1-S3, before first 10 customers are closed

The Problem This Solves

Right now, every prospect who wants to see Corner needs Patrik on a call. That's a hard bottleneck:

  • 30-minute discovery call (Patrik)
  • 30-minute live demo (Patrik)
  • Follow-up (Patrik)

At 10 prospects, that's 10+ hours of Patrik's time just to get to close. It doesn't scale. A self-running demo at aheadofmarket.com/demo removes the bottleneck. Prospects self-qualify and get excited before they ever book a call with Patrik. Warm prospects become much warmer.

The demo is also insurance. If Patrik is on a call and the live product has a glitch, he can fall back to /demo. "Let me show you the full flow." No panic, no apology.

What It Is

A scripted, animated walkthrough of Corner at aheadofmarket.com/demo.

Not: a video. Not a slideshow. Not a live product clone.

Yes: the actual Corner dashboard UI running with pre-loaded data and scripted animations that play like a movie. The prospect feels like they're watching a live system. The magic: it's entirely static. No backend. No Claude API calls. No Supabase queries. Just beautifully scripted UI state with timed transitions.

Think: an Apple product page, but interactive. The kind of thing that makes someone go "wait, is this real?"

The Story It Tells (5 Acts, ~4 minutes)

The demo tells one story: "What Monday morning looks like when you have Corner."

The prospect (a GC or small business owner) opens Corner, sees their agents have already been working overnight, reviews what got done, approves one thing, and closes their laptop. Total time: 4 minutes. That's the dream. The demo proves it's real.

ACT 1: The Office Opens (0:00 -- 0:30)

What the prospect sees:

The isometric office loads. It's morning -- warm light through the windows. Three rooms are lit up, showing activity. The game view zooms gently to center.

A text overlay fades in:

7:42 AM. You just woke up.
Your Corner office has been running since midnight.

After 2 seconds, the overlay fades. The office zooms in on the "Operations" room, which is glowing with activity.

Technical notes:

  • The office uses the existing Canvas2D or Three.js renderer
  • "Morning" state = warm lighting filter on the voxel scene
  • Rooms that are "active" have the pixel art monitors glowing, subtle ambient animation
  • Text overlay: large, centered, dark background at 60% opacity, white text, SF/Helvetica

ACT 2: The Right Now Ticker (0:30 -- 1:00)

What the prospect sees:

The sidebar appears. The "Right Now" pill is lit. Five tasks are listed:

✓ Follow-Up Agent -- Sent invoice reminder to Johnson Electric (7:14 AM)
✓ Schedule Agent -- Confirmed Tuesday's site walk with Martinez (7:22 AM)
✓ Outreach Agent -- Drafted 8 proposal follow-ups, ready for review (7:31 AM)
• Content Agent -- Generating this week's LinkedIn posts (in progress)
• QA Agent -- Reviewing last week's deliverables (in progress)

The two "in progress" items show a subtle pulsing dot. The three completed items have green checkmarks.

A callout tooltip appears next to the list:

"Your agents worked while you slept.
Three things are already done."

After 3 seconds, tooltip fades. The prospect clicks "Outreach Agent -- 8 proposals."

Technical notes:

  • Right Now pill = static pre-populated data
  • No Supabase queries, no API calls
  • The "click" is scripted -- after 3s pause on the proposals task, automatically advance
  • Green checkmarks animate in one at a time (staggered 300ms each)

ACT 3: The Agent Chat (1:00 -- 2:00)

What the prospect sees:

The chat panel slides open. It shows the Outreach Agent's name and avatar. There's a conversation thread:

Outreach Agent [7:31 AM]
"Good morning. I've reviewed your open proposals from last week.
8 were sent 5+ days ago with no response. I've drafted follow-up
messages for each one. Want to review before I send?"

[Review drafts] [Send all] [Remind me later]

The prospect (scripted) clicks "Review drafts." A list expands:

1. Martinez Roofing -- "Following up on our proposal from Tuesday..."
2. Sunbelt Electric -- "Hi Carlos, just checking in on..."
3. Valley Plumbing -- "Tom, wanted to make sure our estimate..."
[+ 5 more]

A "Send all" button appears below. After 2 seconds of the list showing, it pulses.

The prospect (scripted) clicks "Send all." The agent responds:

Outreach Agent [now]
"Done. 8 follow-ups sent. I'll flag any replies that come in."

A quick animation: 8 small email icons fly outward from the chat panel and disappear.

Technical notes:

  • Chat panel = existing component, populated with static data
  • "Send all" click = scripted after 2s
  • Email icons animation = CSS keyframe, 8 divs with staggered delay
  • Agent avatar = Outreach Agent's pixel art portrait

ACT 4: The Game View -- Agents at Work (2:00 -- 3:00)

What the prospect sees:

The sidebar closes. The isometric game view comes back full-width. A spotlight slowly scans the office -- it hits the "Outreach" room first. A speech bubble appears above the Outreach Agent character:

"8 follow-ups sent."

The spotlight moves to the "Schedule" room. Speech bubble:

"Tuesday confirmed."

The spotlight moves to the "Content" room. The agent character is visibly animating (typing, in motion). Speech bubble:

"Working on LinkedIn posts..."

A text overlay fades in over the full scene:

"11 agents. All working.
None of them need managing."

After 3 seconds, overlay fades. The office holds for a moment -- just the ambient game view, agents doing their thing.

Technical notes:

  • Spotlight = CSS radial gradient overlay, moves via animation
  • Speech bubbles = absolutely positioned divs that appear/fade per room
  • "Working" animation on Content Agent = existing idle/active state variants
  • Text overlay uses same style as Act 1

ACT 5: The Close (3:00 -- 4:00)

What the prospect sees:

The game view zooms out slowly. The whole office is visible -- all rooms, all agents, the full picture.

A final text overlay:

"That's Monday morning with Corner.
40 minutes of admin work.
Done before you woke up."

Below the text, two buttons appear:

[Book a free audit →]    [See pricing]

Both buttons are live links (not scripted). The demo ends here.

Technical notes:

  • Zoom out = CSS scale transform, 1s ease-out
  • Final overlay = same style, slightly larger text
  • Buttons = real links to /book and /corner#pricing
  • The demo page does NOT loop. It ends here and stays on the final CTA screen.

Technical Architecture

Route

aheadofmarket.com/demo

Add to vercel.json:

{ "source": "/demo", "destination": "/demo" }

How It Works

The demo is a single React component (DemoPlayer) that:

  1. Loads the existing isometric game view (Canvas2D) with pre-loaded static data
  2. Uses a useEffect timer sequence to advance through scripted states
  3. Each "act" is a state in a demoStep enum
  4. State changes trigger: text overlays, sidebar panels, chat content, spotlight position, speech bubbles
const DEMO_STEPS = [
  'intro',       // Act 1: office loads, morning text
  'right_now',   // Act 2: sidebar, completed tasks
  'agent_chat',  // Act 3: Outreach Agent chat thread
  'game_wide',   // Act 4: spotlight tour of rooms
  'close',       // Act 5: zoom out, final CTA
]

Data Layer

All data is static JSON -- no Supabase, no API calls:

const DEMO_DATA = {
  client_name: "Peak Construction",
  tasks: [
    { agent: "Follow-Up", text: "Sent invoice reminder to Johnson Electric", time: "7:14 AM", done: true },
    { agent: "Schedule", text: "Confirmed Tuesday site walk with Martinez", time: "7:22 AM", done: true },
    { agent: "Outreach", text: "Drafted 8 proposal follow-ups, ready for review", time: "7:31 AM", done: true },
    { agent: "Content", text: "Generating this week's LinkedIn posts", time: "now", done: false },
    { agent: "QA", text: "Reviewing last week's deliverables", time: "now", done: false },
  ],
  proposals: [
    { name: "Martinez Roofing", preview: "Following up on our proposal from Tuesday..." },
    { name: "Sunbelt Electric", preview: "Hi Carlos, just checking in on..." },
    { name: "Valley Plumbing", preview: "Tom, wanted to make sure our estimate..." },
    // 5 more...
  ],
  rooms: [
    { id: "operations", label: "Operations", active: true },
    { id: "outreach", label: "Outreach", active: true },
    { id: "schedule", label: "Schedule", active: true },
    { id: "content", label: "Content", active: true, working: true },
    { id: "qa", label: "QA", active: true, working: true },
  ]
}

Controls

The demo runs automatically. No interaction required. But add a simple scrubber at the bottom:

[Act 1] [Act 2] [Act 3] [Act 4] [Act 5]  [▶ Replay]

Clicking an act jumps directly to it. Clicking Replay restarts from Act 1. This lets prospects revisit specific moments or re-watch.

No Autoplay Gotcha

On mobile, autoplay animations can feel jarring. Add a "Start demo" screen before Act 1:

  • Shows the game view in its final state (zoom-out, all rooms visible)
  • Overlay: "See Corner in action. 4 minutes."
  • One centered button: [Start demo →]
  • On click, Act 1 begins

Copy for Each Act

Act 1 overlay

7:42 AM. You just woke up.
Your Corner office has been running since midnight.

Act 2 tooltip

Your agents worked while you slept.
Three things are already done.

Act 4 overlay

11 agents. All working.
None of them need managing.

Act 5 overlay

That's Monday morning with Corner.
40 minutes of admin work.
Done before you woke up.

Final CTAs

[Book a free audit →]    [See pricing]

Elmo QA Checklist

Before this ships:

  • Demo plays through all 5 acts with no errors on desktop
  • Demo plays through all 5 acts on iPhone (no layout breaks)
  • "Start demo" screen shows on mobile, not desktop
  • Scrubber controls jump to correct acts
  • Replay button restarts from Act 1
  • Final CTAs link correctly (/book and /corner#pricing)
  • No API calls in Network tab (all data is static)
  • Acts 2 and 3 feel like real interactions (not obviously scripted)
  • Text overlays are readable at all viewport sizes (min 18px)
  • The game view loads and is recognizable as an isometric office

What This Unlocks

When /demo is live:

  • The /corner landing page gets a "See it in action" button that links here
  • Every outreach text can include: "You can actually see it working here: aheadofmarket.com/demo"
  • Prospects can share the link with their business partner before a call
  • Patrik can use this as a fallback if the live product has a glitch mid-demo

This is Phase 2 of the sales plan. It's the content layer that makes the website convert without Patrik being present.

Dependencies

  • S1-S3 must ship first (demo uses same game view; no auth bypass risk since demo is all static)
  • Steffen: the voxel office needs a "morning" lighting state (warm, not the default blue/gray)
  • Bobby: builds DemoPlayer component from this spec
  • Elmo: QA run before launch
